analysis_scope: Shared two-resistor DUT; deterministic Linear S and explicitly identified RF System signal observations.

provenance.reference: Installed SystemVue 2023 help; local read-only review

sources.title: Linear Analysis
sources.fact_summary: Computes schematic S and noise parameters; the overview says nonlinear parts are linearized at a DC operating point. This overview alone does not prove arbitrary device support.

sources.title: Linear Analysis Output
sources.fact_summary: F is the frequency vector; S is normalized to schematic port ZPORT; CS is the S-form noise correlation matrix; ZPORT contains impedances from port parts. Two-port shortcuts include S11/S12/S21/S22, Zin1/Zin2, and NF when noise is enabled.

sources.title: Port Impedance Usage
sources.fact_summary: Linear design ports are sequential starting at 1. Balanced ports and complex port terminations are described; complex impedance can be supplied directly or from one-port data.

sources.title: Linear Analysis Properties
sources.fact_summary: Calculate Noise enables CS; the frequency range has explicit units and sweep choice. Analysis temperature can be overridden by a part Ta.

sources.title: RF Design Kit Spectrasys
sources.fact_summary: Spectrasys is the RF architecture analysis with spectral propagation, mismatch, nonlinear behavioral and X-parameter support.

sources.title: Getting Started with Spectrasys
sources.fact_summary: States that Spectrasys supports all linear models and behavioral nonlinear models. The tutorial adds an RF System Analysis and uses a fixed attenuator among its RF chain components.

sources.title: Channel Power (CP)
sources.fact_summary: Main-channel integrated total power includes signal, intermod, harmonic, noise and phase-noise spectra in all travel directions. First-path-node power uses the internal source plane rather than the delivered first-stage input. Requires Add Power Measurements.

sources.title: Desired Channel Power (DCP)
sources.fact_summary: Main-channel integrated power includes only desired signals originating at the path beginning and traveling forward; other signal classes and reverse travel are excluded. First-node value uses the internal source plane. Requires power or voltage measurements.

sources.title: Channel Voltage (CV)
sources.fact_summary: Described as main-channel peak voltage, default dBV; includes all spectrum types and all directions. Not supported for nonlinear circuit models such as X parameters. Requires Add Voltage Measurements.

sources.title: Channel Noise Voltage (CNV)
sources.fact_summary: Described as main-channel peak noise voltage, default dBV; only noise and forward path direction. Not supported for nonlinear circuit models such as X parameters. Requires Add Voltage Measurements.

sources.title: Desired Channel Voltage (DCV)
sources.fact_summary: Main-channel desired peak voltage, default dBV; only desired signals in the forward path direction. Requires Add Voltage Measurements; nonlinear circuit models are excluded.

sources.title: Node Noise Voltage (NNV)
sources.fact_summary: Peak node noise voltage includes in-band and out-of-band noise; only forward path noise. Distinct from band-limited CNV.

sources.title: Input Impedance (ZIN)
sources.fact_summary: Simulated input impedance at the path node, evaluated at the path center frequency, independent of channel bandwidth. Not defined using signal-spectrum selection.

sources.title: Output Impedance (ZOUT)
sources.fact_summary: Simulated output impedance at the path node, evaluated at the path center frequency, independent of channel bandwidth. Not defined using signal-spectrum selection.

sources.title: Stage Input Impedance (SZIN)
sources.fact_summary: User-entered stage input impedance; stages without this parameter use 50 ohms. Associated with a stage rather than the path node.

sources.title: Stage Output Impedance (SZOUT)
sources.fact_summary: User-entered stage output impedance; stages without this parameter use 50 ohms. Associated with a stage rather than the path node.

sources.title: Desired Channel Resistance (DCR)
sources.fact_summary: Average real part of desired-signal impedance in the main channel and forward path direction, not impedance magnitude.

sources.title: Path Measurement Overview
sources.fact_summary: Path measurements integrate grouped spectra over channel center and bandwidth. GAIN is stage-output DCP divided by stage-input DCP; CGAIN uses DCP at the source. A CW spectrum has 1 Hz width; integrating only 0.5 Hz yields 3 dB less power.

sources.title: Node Measurements Along Path
sources.fact_summary: Optional path datasets save F/V/P/Z for named nodes and groups such as Desired, Noise and PhaseNoise. The grouping paragraph describes the path direction; this generic wording must not override the CP-specific all-directions definition.

sources.title: Specifying Paths
sources.fact_summary: Arbitrary architectures and multiple paths are supported. Start/end and optional through-nodes define the shortest route; equal-length ties can depend on component creation order. Record the resolved route.

sources.title: Add / Edit Path Dialog Box
sources.fact_summary: Normal path uses nonmodulated schematic sources. Allow path to begin on internal node changes desired classification. Power, voltage and detailed P/V/Z output switches are separate. Channel frequency changes through translation devices; explicit ordered through-nodes disambiguate routes.

sources.title: VSWR and Mismatch Loss
sources.fact_summary: Saved node voltage is a transmitted voltage associated with a source and travel direction, and its spectrum power uses the load impedance seen in that direction. Opposite-travel spectra can have different loads. First-node DCP/GAIN/CGAIN source references include the input mismatch correction.

sources.title: Gain and Impedance
sources.fact_summary: Model gain parameters use S21; path gains use operating-power gain with a source/first-stage mismatch correction. Model S21 and path gain are different quantities.

sources.title: Resistor Part
sources.fact_summary: Identifies the ideal non-inductive resistor and lists RES among the associated models.

sources.title: Resistor (RES)
sources.fact_summary: R is resistance in ohms, default 50; optional Ta overrides analysis ambient temperature. The part is a lumped resistor.

sources.title: Attenuator Part
sources.fact_summary: Lists ATTN_Linear as a behavioral attenuator alongside other nonlinear and S-parameter based options.

sources.title: ATTN_Linear
sources.fact_summary: Parameters include L in dB, Zref, ZIN, ZOUT and Ta. Notes distinguish user input/output impedances, loss dependence for large impedance ratios, and use of the linear portion outside Spectrasys. Do not infer a matched four-S matrix from L alone.

provenance.stored_content: Only independently written factual summaries, page identifiers and hashes; no vendor HTML or installed example files.

evidence_layers.help_definition: The 27 local pages define analysis outputs, spectra, directions, reference planes and device identity. They do not prove this candidate has run.
evidence_layers.independent_oracle: Elementary series-resistor circuit equations. Production code and vendor results are not used to construct expected numbers.
evidence_layers.implementation: Existing native C++17 typed APIs and behavioral SDK; no new acquisition adapter or runtime invocation is supplied by this plan.
evidence_layers.unresolved: Vendor export identity and the additional semantic questions listed below remain gates, not accepted equivalences.

fixture.reference_ground: Common physical ground; record actual schematic reference.

linear_analysis.S_index_convention: row=response port, column=excited port; capture source array ordering explicitly

channel.purpose: RF integrated path measurements only; captures the entire documented 1-Hz CW spectrum. Not used by Linear or deterministic circuit equations.

rf_system_analysis.noise_off_absence_policy: Record presence or absence; absent/omitted noise output is not an accepted zero-noise measurement and does not fail this signal-only minimum.
capture_settings: source and load impedance and units

oracle.classification: Independent analytic physical circuit, not vendor-observed data.
oracle.port_current_convention: Native current enters the named device; R1/p1 and R2/p1 are -I. Vendor RF-path current direction is unconfirmed.
oracle.impedance_warning: Loaded V/I is neither ZPORT nor an automatically identified ZIN/ZOUT/SZIN/SZOUT/DCR.
oracle.peak_warning: sqrt(2)*abs(V_RMS) applies here to a deterministic single CW; this plan does not impose it on integrated noise.

required_before_numeric_comparison: frequency and channel bounds where relevant
phase reference for any complex voltage
observable_identity_gate.numeric_format: Raw complex real/imaginary values with enough precision for binary64 round-trip; a screenshot or truncated displayed value is insufficient.
observable_identity_gate.unit_conversions: Convert dBm to W only for confirmed referenced power; convert dBV to V only for confirmed peak-voltage observable in this plan. Preserve original values and units.
observable_identity_gate.identity_prohibition: Numerical proximity to the oracle must never establish the observable identity.

comparison_policy.justification: A passive nonresonant resistor chain has benign conditioning. These experiment-policy bounds allow implementation and unit-conversion rounding while distinguishing the reference-plane, RMS/peak and sign errors at issue. They are not a measured or promised Keysight accuracy.

eligible_comparisons.required_plane: internal source available power, not DUT delivered input

eligible_comparisons.required_identity: forward desired CW delivered to the sole load; complete main-channel integration
peak voltage of the same forward desired CW; dBV or linear peak V explicitly confirmed

diagnostic_not_scored: CP and CV at every node
other port V/P until directional identity is established
comparison_policy.completion_rule: Every required identity and eligible comparison must be present and pass to accept this minimum; otherwise report pass/fail/not_comparable/missing/not_run individually and do not claim overall compatibility. Diagnostics do not turn into acceptance points.
comparison_policy.change_control: Insufficient export precision requires reacquisition. Do not relax gates after viewing differences; any changed design or policy requires a new justified plan revision and fresh acquisition. No historical thresholds are changed.

native_mapping.model: StaticSParameterModel and owning ModelAdapter, one shared connection list
native_mapping.linear: analyze_linear at 100e6; external ports R1/p0 then R2/p1
native_mapping.device_sources: R1/p0 source=sqrt(0.001), all other source entries zero
native_mapping.boundary_reflections: source and load reflection=0 at 50-ohm references
native_mapping.optional_chain_helper: analyze_linear_path independently names source_available_w, input_accepted_w, load_delivered_w and transducer_gain; it is not automatically vendor GAIN/CGAIN.
native_mapping.existing_example_limit: The current example uses 1 and 2 GHz. It demonstrates the API pattern and analytic circuit but does not execute this 100-MHz vendor experiment.
native_mapping.missing: No plan-specific vendor exporter or general CP/CV/CNV compatibility implementation is provided.

open_questions: Exact machine-export dataset names, dimensions and unit metadata must be captured without guessing.
The general node grouping page describes path-forward groups while the CP-specific definition includes all directions; retain both raw groups and named measurements.
ZIN/ZOUT suppressed-source boundary conditions and looking direction are not fully specified by the reviewed pages.
CV/CNV pages mix peak with average/integrated wording; general stochastic RMS mapping remains unverified.
RF-path current direction and coherent complex-voltage aggregation remain unverified.
Do not infer a full matched ATTN_Linear four-S/noise law from L; RES avoids that unresolved model mapping in this first candidate.
follow_up_not_in_this_plan: separate coordinate-reference changes and physical source/load impedance changes
noise-enabled reference experiment with its own normalization and tolerance policy
